data.description:
## Context
F12 makes committed help available for every visible route that is not retired and uses those artifacts to generate the CLI reference. Manual review found writing-guideline violations in newly exposed help and reference text. The affected output inherits parser descriptions and help strings that predate the documentation policy. Examples occur in help for `verify-completion`, `sign-review`, `explain`, `verify-identity`, and `remote-cert`, along with overview summaries. F08A and F10 do not provide general coverage for parser-owned CLI help. The operator rejected character restrictions and other mechanical prose enforcement.

## Proposed remediation
- Inventory writing-guideline violations in committed CLI help and the generated CLI reference.
- Trace every affected generated line to its parser description, option help, or other source string.
- Rewrite the source strings manually for an external user audience while preserving command meaning, technical identifiers, and argparse behavior.
- Regenerate committed help and the CLI reference through the existing generators.
- Use drift checks and content-specific behavior tests. Do not add a character gate, banned-word scanner, punctuation scanner, or similar mechanical enforcement.
- Record any wording that cannot be changed because it is an interoperability token, syntax form, quoted third-party value, or stable machine contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The affected committed help and CLI reference prose conforms to the project writing guidelines.
- [ ] Each changed generated line is corrected at its maintained source.
- [ ] Command semantics, syntax, technical identifiers, and exit behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] The help and CLI-reference drift checks pass.
- [ ] Focused CLI help contracts pass.
- [ ] No mechanical character or prose enforcement is introduced.
data.title: F20 align generated CLI help with documentation writing guidelines
